issues.failure_explanation: The eigenproblems define λ as the Laplacian eigenvalue, so separation requires β²+λ=k². The stated propagation constants instead impose β²+λ²=k², while the reconstruction proof again uses λ as the unsquared eigenvalue. Consequently the purported modal fields generally have Helmholtz residual proportional to λ−λ² and are not Maxwell solutions. The same incompatibility occurs for TM modes.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Keep λ as the Laplacian eigenvalue, replace the dispersion relations by β=√(k²−λ), and interpret the numerical variable r through r²=λ. Alternatively, consistently change both eigenproblems and reconstruction denominators to a squared-eigenfrequency convention.
issues.overall_effect: The constructed mode profiles and their use as Maxwell solutions in the modal iteration analysis are not justified with the definitions as written.
issues.title: Propagation constants use incompatible powers of the transverse eigenvalues
issues.why_classification: A consistent spectral-parameter convention repairs the construction locally and preserves the intended modal and iteration results without a new lemma.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: This time, the expression does depend on the sign of $\beta$.

issues.failure_explanation: The source establishes equality only of the tangential TM traces, not of the full forward and backward profiles. Their longitudinal components must change relative sign. Multiplying the forward profile by the backward exponential therefore does not produce a backward Maxwell mode: in the stretched coordinate its divergence is −2iβ times its nonzero longitudinal component. Thus the displayed finite-PML field is not a Maxwell solution.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We remind that the eigenvalue problem \eqref{eq:ev} has an infinite countable set of solutions

issues.failure_explanation: The valid per-mode limit supplies no uniform gap below one over the infinitely many modes. This can fail even with nonsingular modal matrices: put β_i=iγ_i with γ_i→∞, s=L+δ, choose 0<c_i↑1, t_i=c_i e^{γ_iδ}≠1, and set the TE transmission eigenvalue λ_i=γ_i(1+t_i)/(1−t_i). The coefficient formulas give q_i=max(|a_i+b_i|,|a_i−b_i|)=(c_i+e^{−γ_i s})/(1+c_i e^{−γ_i s})<1, but a_i→1 and b_i→0. Even for N=2 the modal radii therefore approach one, so the full modal problem has no common geometric convergence factor below one.

failure_location.quote: If this convergence factor is stricly less than $1$ for all modes, we say that the method will scale.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Require a uniform modal bound sup q_i<1. Use the block structure to obtain a uniform-in-N contraction bound, and verify the high-mode tail for the specified impedance/PML operators before inferring full-problem scalability.
issues.overall_effect: The theorem establishes modewise asymptotics, not the advertised full-problem scalability criterion for the general diagonal class.
issues.title: Pointwise modal contraction does not give a full-problem convergence rate
issues.why_classification: A contained uniform-modal argument and a strengthened criterion suffice for comparable results, but the pointwise condition cannot be retained as the general guarantee.

issues.failure_explanation: For a real β>0, let x=a_j−d in the left layer. The stated stretch gives x̃−a_j=−d+iσd, so a left-going wave becomes exp(−iβ(x̃−a_j))=exp(iβd+βσd), which grows rather than decays. Its terminated-layer reflection factor has modulus exp(2βσℓ). In the infinite-layer limit the left boundary selects the opposite admittance from the outgoing one, while the right layer selects the outgoing admittance. These are not the common transparent transmission conditions assumed in the proposition.

failure_location.quote: In the case of an infinite PML, $\ell = +\infty$, which corresponds to the perfect ``Dirichlet To Neumann'' operator $\mathcal{T}$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use x̃=x+iσ(x−a_j) in the left layer and repeat the elementary left-boundary reflection calculation, thereby obtaining the same outgoing transmission eigenvalues as on the right.
issues.overall_effect: The geometrically defined infinite PML does not supply the two outgoing DtN maps required for the claimed Schwarz nilpotency; its limiting local problems can instead be singular.
issues.title: The left PML stretches outgoing waves in the amplifying direction
issues.why_classification: A local correction of the stretching direction restores the intended PML and preserves the N-step guarantee without a new proof architecture.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We should note that for $\sigma > 0$ and $\ell \rightarrow +\infty$ then $e^{2 \imath \beta^{\rm T}_i (1 + \imath \sigma)\ell} \rightarrow 0$

The allowed complex coefficients can give, for example, β=1−i; with σ=1/2 the modulus is exp(ℓ), so the asserted limit is false even in the right layer. No attenuation or square-root-branch hypothesis excludes this case.
